segments: 2. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And a kor of wheat was sold for four hundred gold dinars,
and a thousand Baghdadi pounds of dates for sixty dinars.
And for morsels and loaves of bread, courtyards, vineyards, and gardens were sold.
And from the dung of horses and donkeys, people would pick out grains of barley and eat them.
And many women were caught who had roasted their children in the oven to eat them,
and they were executed.
And many perished in that famine,
and were eaten by dogs,
for lack of anyone to bury them.
And in the year 1260
of the Greeks
(949 of our Lord? which is the year 337
of the Arabs):
The Romans went out into the territory of the Arabs.
And Sayf al-Dawla, the emir of Hims and Aleppo, met them,
and the Arabs were defeated.
And the Romans took Germanicia, which is Marash,
and reached as far as Tarsus,
and they killed, plundered, and departed.
And in the year 339
of the Arabs:
Sayf al-Dawla gathered thirty thousand men, both horsemen and foot soldiers,
and entered the territory of the Romans,
and took great spoil.
And as he was leaving,
the Romans overtook him,
and seized the passes (clisuras) against him,
and killed and captured the entire force that was with him,
and recovered the captives.
And Sayf al-Dawla himself escaped with only a few men,
while his men, horses, mules, treasures, and possessions were lost.
And in this year, the Black Stone was brought back, the one in the sanctuary of Mecca,
by which those who go to pray are blessed,
after twenty-three years of having been seized by the Qarmatians, the tyrants in the South;
they returned it, however, for fifty thousand dinars which were given to them.
And they brought it broken in two,
and they fastened it with silver bands until today.
And at that time there was plenty,
and twenty Baghdadi pounds of bread were sold for one zuz.
And in the year 1258
(1268? {OCR?}) of the Greeks,
which is the year
of the Arabs:
The Romans went out by sea to Tarsus,
and burned many villages,
and killed one thousand eight hundred fighting men of the Arabs,
and departed.
And a little later, Sayf al-Dawla gathered an army,
and entered the territory of the Romans,
and reached as far as Charsianon,
and took captives, burned, and killed.
And he came to Adana, a city of Cilicia,
